pages.text: Nell lived above a workshop at the end of Cobble Lane. Her grandmother, Mrs. Hobbs, was an inventor. The workshop was packed with gears, springs, bolts and tools.
On the top shelf sat a clockwork fox. It was made of copper, with green glass eyes and a long brass tail. Nell had never seen it move.
"It stopped working before you were born," said Mrs. Hobbs. "Something is missing inside it, but I never found out what."
That night, Nell could not sleep. She crept down the steps with a lamp. She lifted the fox from the shelf and set it on the bench.
She opened a little hatch in its chest. Inside were tiny wheels and a spring, all still. In the middle was an empty slot, as thin as a coin.
The next morning, Nell made a plan. She would search the whole workshop for the missing part. She began with the boxes on the shelves.
The first box had nails. The second had buttons. The third had a pile of old letters tied with string. One letter had a picture of a fox on it.
Nell unfolded the letter. It said: "The heart of the fox is hidden where the clock tells no time."
Nell frowned. Every clock in the workshop ticked. Then she looked up. High on the wall was a clock with no hands at all.
She dragged a stool across the floor and climbed up. Behind the clock face was a small copper disk, shaped like a heart.
Nell slid the copper heart into the empty slot. Click! For a second, nothing happened. Then the tiny wheels began to spin.
The fox lifted its head. Its green eyes began to glow. It stretched its legs and swished its long brass tail.
Nell gasped. "Grandmother! Come quick!" Mrs. Hobbs rushed in, still in her slippers. Her mouth fell open.
"You found it," she said softly. "Your grandfather hid that heart to keep the fox safe. I thought it was lost for good."
The fox trotted over to Nell and sat at her feet. "I think it likes you," said Mrs. Hobbs. "It needs a name."
Nell grinned. "I will call it Pepper," she said. And from that day on, Pepper the clockwork fox followed her everywhere.

glossary.def: a person who makes something new that did not exist before
gears and springs that make something move when you wind it up

questions.q: What was missing from the fox?
What does "crept" mean in "She crept down the steps"?
Why did the clue say "where the clock tells no time"?
options: The clock was broken in half
